claim: Selective or controlled retention of a therapeutic agent in the CSF compartment while maintaining therapeutic-safety-grade CSF drainage through the eShunt.
rationale: V8.6 proved retention is the primary mechanism (288% alone vs 2% for release alone). Spatial separation is secondary. The flagship is RETENTION WHILE DRAINING.
independent_claim: A method of controlling therapeutic exposure in the cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) of a patient via an endovascular CSF-to-venous shunt, comprising: (a) delivering a therapeutic agent into the CSF via the shunt; (b) selectively retaining said therapeutic agent in the CSF compartment via a size-selective retention element that permits CSF passage while retaining molecules above a molecular weight threshold; (c) maintaining clinically adequate CSF drainage through said shunt throughout the retention period; wherein therapeutic exposure in the CSF and adjacent tissue is increased relative to unretained delivery while CSF drainage is preserved.
novelty_basis: L4 (selective retention) not found in 15+ charted patents. L5 (controlled residence) not found. L7 (drainage preservation fail-safe) not found.
